the uptake of copper by roots and leaves is associated to different symptoms of toxicity in sweet orange trees.
the mechanisms of Cu stress alleviation in citrus trees are different after metal uptake by roots or leaves.

a better understanding of the mechanisms involved in citrus responses to Cu toxicity, and it will contribute to develop new management strategies to prevent and reduce Cu toxicity in citrus orchards.
the mechanisms involved in the Cu toxicity in citrus, which can help to improve the management strategies of citrus orchards.
the mechanisms of Cu stress alleviation in citrus plants after metal uptake by roots or leaves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
citrus is a metal hyperaccumulator plant, which can accumulate high amounts of Cu in the roots, but this plant species is also sensitive to excess Cu.
Cu excess is a problem for the citrus industry, and that Cu(OH) 2 is the best source of foliar application to avoid Cu toxicity in the citrus plants.
Cu is a phytotoxic element to citrus plants, but the symptoms are more evident when the metal is foliar sprayed, mainly as Cu sulfate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Cu excess toxicity is not only a function of the metal concentration in the soil, but the way the metal is absorbed and distributed within the plant, and the way it interacts with the plant metabolism.
Cu excess in citrus plants is more dangerous when the metal is foliar absorbed as sulfate, since the metal is accumulated in leaves and it is not easily eliminated.
the Cu stress alleviation mechanisms in citrus trees are more related to metal exclusion than detoxification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cu excess damages the plant growth and metabolism, regardless of the metal uptake pathway.

the foliar application of Cu(OH) 2 as a fungicide can be used in citrus orchards without causing damages on plant growth or oxidative status, but the application of Cu as sulfate must be avoided to prevent the damages caused to plant growth and metabolism.
Cu uptake via roots or leaves can cause damages on plant growth, metabolism, and oxidative stress, which are dependent on the amount and form of Cu applied to the soil or sprayed to leaves.
